b.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's n8n on a 2 GB Ubuntu LTS server at https://n8n.harvestlane.example.

  1. Server: SSH key login, provider backups on, ufw allowing only OpenSSH, 80 and 443. DNS: an A record for n8n pointing at the server's IP.
  2. Files in ~/n8n, from Card 3: docker-compose.yml (n8n with no published ports, Caddy on 80 and 443), Caddyfile, and: 
    # .env  (private: never commit it)
DOMAIN=n8n.harvestlane.example
N8N_VERSION=2.x.x        # the exact number you picked from the release notes
N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY=****  # generated; a copy is in the password manager
TZ_NAME=Africa/Lagos
  3. docker compose up -d, wait for "Editor is now accessible", create the owner with two-factor login.
  4. Move: import HL · Morning weather → Sheet and HL · Error alerts; recreate the Google and Telegram credentials (they don't travel); set the weather workflow's error workflow; publish both; unpublish the laptop copies.

Evidence:

  • Browser padlock on https://n8n.harvestlane.example.
  • Server Executions showing the 06:30 run, with a note that the laptop was off, and that day's HL Weather row.
  • The alarm test alert on your phone, whose run link starts with https://n8n.harvestlane.example/, not localhost.
  • Proof that http://SERVER-IP:5678 doesn't load from outside.
mistakes: Leaving -p 5678:5678 or a firewall gap, so the login page is open on http://server-ip:5678.
Not setting N8N_WEBHOOK_URL, so webhook and run links still say localhost.
Forgetting to unpublish the laptop copies, so the weather row arrives twice.
Keeping the only copy of the encryption key on the server.
b.pass: A padlock on the learner's own domain, an automatic 06:30 run in the server's Executions on a day the laptop was off, and an alarm-test alert whose link points at the public https address.
b.redo: Send it back if HTTPS is missing, port 5678 is reachable from outside, the run came from the laptop, or workflows run in two places.

s.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's private repo harvestlane-n8n, with HL · Backup workflows → GitHub built as in the solved problem (02:00 daily, Get many workflows, Code to make workflows/<name>.json, Edit a file, error output → Create a file). It uses a fine-grained token for that one repo only, and is connected to HL · Error alerts.

The change test: on Tuesday, Tolu's builder lowers the weather workflow's rain threshold from 60 to 50 in the advice expression, saves and publishes.

Commit (GitHub history)What it shows
nightly backup 2026-10-06First run: 7 files created (via the error output → Create a file)
nightly backup 2026-10-07Files updated in place
nightly backup 2026-10-08HL_Morning_weather_Sheet.json diff: >= 60 changed to >= 50

Rollback:

  1. In GitHub, open that file's history, pick the 2026-10-07 version and download the raw file.
  2. In n8n, open HL · Morning weather → Sheet, ⋮ → Import from File, choose the download. The canvas now shows the old version (threshold 60). Credentials reconnect because they're referenced by ID on the same server.
  3. Execute workflow: one row arrives with the 60% rule. Save and publish.
  4. The next 02:00 commit shows the threshold back at 60, which proves the loop works both ways.

Submit: a screenshot of the repo file list (every workflow present), the commit history with at least three daily commits, the diff, and the Executions entry for the restored version. Check that no .env or token appears anywhere in the repo.
mistakes: Using a classic all-repo GitHub token instead of a fine-grained one limited to the backup repo.
Making the repo public, or committing the .env file alongside the workflows.
Forgetting the error output → Create a file, so new workflows are never backed up.
Claiming a rollback without running the restored version.
s.pass: A private repo containing every workflow, a daily commit history showing the learner's change as a diff, and a successful execution of an older version imported from GitHub.
s.redo: Send it back if workflows are missing from the repo, there is no visible diff, or the rollback wasn't executed.

g.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's one-page runbook, written for a tired person at 3 a.m. The IP is a documentation example.

HARVEST LANE n8n RUNBOOK  (updated 2026-10-12)
Server    VPS, Europe region, 2 GB, Ubuntu LTS, IP 203.0.113.24
Domain    n8n.harvestlane.example (A record at the registrar)
Log in    ssh deploy@203.0.113.24 with the key "hl-ops" from the
          password manager vault "Harvest Lane Ops"
Files     ~/n8n/.env, docker-compose.yml, Caddyfile
Key       NOT here. Vault "Harvest Lane Ops", item "n8n encryption key"
Restart   cd ~/n8n && docker compose restart n8n
Logs      docker compose logs --tail 200 n8n
Health    https://n8n.harvestlane.example/healthz should say ok
Backups   1 provider snapshots (nightly)  2 CLI exports in the volume
          (backups/ folder)  3 GitHub repo harvestlane-n8n
Restore   new server, install Docker, copy the 3 files, put the key
          in .env BEFORE first start, restore the volume (or import
          workflows and credentials), start, test the weather workflow
Roll back version  restore the backup taken before the update,
          set N8N_VERSION back, docker compose pull && up -d
Contacts  Tolu (owner) · automation builder · host support page

Test: Tolu's operations assistant, who has never used SSH, was given only this page.

TaskResultGot stuck onRunbook change
Restart n8nDone in 9 minutesWhere the SSH key file goes on her laptopAdded a "first time on a new laptop" line
Find the latest backupFound last night's GitHub commitDidn't know the repo was private, so the link failed while signed outAdded "sign in as harvestlane-ops first"

She asked no questions on the second attempt.

Go-live checklist: all 13 items ticked, including the restore tested on a fresh server and the runbook shared with a second person.

Submit: the runbook (v1 and v2), the tester's notes, and the 100% checklist screenshot.
mistakes: Pasting the encryption key or passwords into the runbook instead of saying where they are kept.
Testing the runbook on yourself or on someone who already knows the server.
Writing "restore from backup" without the order of steps (key in .env before first start).
Ticking checklist items such as the restore test without actually doing them.
g.pass: A one-page runbook with every required section and no secrets, notes showing a second person restarted n8n and found the latest backup using only the page, an updated version fixing what they got stuck on, and a 100% go-live checklist.
g.redo: Send it back if secrets appear, the tester needed help, sections are missing, or the checklist isn't complete.
